title: Lynn White of Long Beach, California, who lost an eviction jury trial with a lawyer, may have overturned the eviction on appeal with ChatGPT and Perplexity, which she used to find procedural errors and draft it, avoiding roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in back rent
summary: Long Beach tenant Lynn White used ChatGPT and Perplexity to overturn her eviction on appeal, avoiding about $55,000 in penalties, per NBC.
account: Lynn White, a small music production business owner living in a Long Beach, California, trailer park, was allegedly behind on rent and facing eviction. Represented by a lawyer from a local tenant advocacy network, she lost a jury trial. To appeal, she argued that Los Angeles Covid-era rules allowed a 12-month rent deferral. She gave her documents to ChatGPT and the AI search engine Perplexity. She had them find procedural errors by the judge, research the law and draft her court responses. NBC News reported on 8 October 2025 that, after several months of litigation, she overturned the eviction. It said she avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in overdue rent. No court, docket or ruling date is given.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant for answering questions and drafting text. Perplexity is an AI search engine. Using them to research law, spot procedural errors and draft filings is within that general purpose. Neither is built as a legal service. The same NBC report documents litigants sanctioned for AI-invented case citations.
system: ChatGPT (paid plan, $20 a month) and Perplexity Pro ($20 a month)
model_version: Not reported; NBC News says White moved from the free ChatGPT tier to the $20-a-month plan and used Perplexity Pro, without naming model versions

ratings.reason: By her account to NBC News, White kept her home after losing at trial with a lawyer. She avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and more than $18,000 in overdue rent. That is life-changing for one person. But the figures and outcome rest on her account, and no court record is cited.

ai_role.statement: White told NBC News that she gave ChatGPT her documents and case details. She said it and Perplexity identified procedural errors by the judge, researched the applicable law and drafted her court responses. She said she could never have won the appeal without AI. No court document, opposing-party or judicial account of what decided the appeal is cited. So the tools' contribution relative to the Covid-era rent-deferral rules she invoked and her own advocacy is not established.

fields.account: Lynn White, a small music production business owner living in a Long Beach, California, trailer park, was allegedly behind on rent and facing eviction. Represented by a lawyer from a local tenant advocacy network, she lost a jury trial. To appeal, she argued that Los Angeles Covid-era rules allowed a 12-month rent deferral. She gave her documents to ChatGPT and the AI search engine Perplexity. She had them find procedural errors by the judge, research the law and draft her court responses. NBC News reported on 8 October 2025 that, after several months of litigation, she overturned the eviction. It said she avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in overdue rent. No court, docket or ruling date is given.

fields.account: Lynn White, a small music production business owner living in a Long Beach, California, trailer park, was allegedly behind on rent and facing eviction. Represented by a lawyer from a local tenant advocacy network, she lost a jury trial. To appeal, she argued that Los Angeles Covid-era rules allowed a 12-month rent deferral. She gave her documents to ChatGPT and the AI search engine Perplexity. She had them find procedural errors by the judge, research the law and draft her court responses. NBC News reported on 8 October 2025 that, after several months of litigation, she overturned the eviction. It said she avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in overdue rent. No court, docket or ruling date is given.
